title: microadmin-assembler-for-safe-interactive-remediations
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight 'Microadmin Assembler' service that turns curated runbook fragments and admin utility snippets into idempotent, interactive remediation flows that can be invoked from the support console or programmatically by alerting playbooks. The goal is to reduce mean time to remediate for common support scenarios while preserving safety guarantees (RBAC, dry-run, undo checkpoints) and clear provenance.
acceptance_criteria: Assembler can compose a templated remediation flow from a runbook fragment + context and return a dry-run execution plan
Flows are idempotent: running the same flow twice with the same context produces no side-effect duplication
Support console can preview, approve, and execute assembled flows with per-step audit metadata
Automated playbooks can invoke assembled flows with scoped credentials and auto-rollback on failure
End-to-end telemetry (user, flow-template, inputs, outcomes, tokens) is emitted to ops-telemetry for analytics
proposed_solution: Implement an assembly service that: (1) accepts a runbook fragment identifier and runtime context, (2) synthesizes an ordered list of typed steps with preconditions and idempotency checks, (3) produces a signed dry-run manifest for console preview, and (4) exposes execution endpoints that apply per-step gating (RBAC, approval, rate-limits) and rollback hooks. Use existing runbook snippet registry for templates and extend snippet schema with 'compensation' and 'precheck' fields. Execution should run in an ephemeral 'runlet' with limited credentials and emit a compact provenance record to the ledger service.
tech_notes: Add 'compensation' and 'precheck' fields to snippet schema (stringified command + expected invariant)
Leverage existing admin-runlet sandbox to run staged steps; ensure network egress disabled by default for high-risk steps
Design a canonical dry-run manifest format (JSON-LD or similar) that the console can render without executing
Plan to reuse ops-telemetry pipeline and add new event types: flow.assembled, flow.dryrun, flow.executed, flow.compensated
Prefer synchronous assembly for console use (sub-500ms) and async batch for heavy contextual enrichment (e.g., long artifact lookups)
Use short-lived service tokens from vault; require audit-log hook per execution
rollout_plan: Phase 1: PoC - assembler returns dry-run manifests for 5 curated snippets; console preview only (internal QA)
Phase 2: Beta - enable live execution for ops-internal with strict RBAC and manual approvals
Phase 3: GA - open to support team and allow automated invocation from alert playbooks with rate-limits
Phase 4: Expand snippet library and add template param validation and safety heuristics
comments: 2026-01-19 - Asha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes attached. Decided to scope to five high-frequency remediations for the PoC: disk cleanup, service restart, config rollbacks, certificate rotate, and user session kill. Agreed to use existing snippet registry as the source of truth.

2026-01-26 - Daniel Kim: Spike complete. Prototype can assemble a 3-step flow (precheck -> action -> compensation) for the restart snippet. Dry-run manifest rendered in console mockup. Perf is ~180ms for simple contexts.

2026-02-10 - Security Review Request: Submitted initial design to security for credential handling and compensation semantics. Pending review. Noted requirement: all execution tokens must be ephemeral and tied to invocation ID.
2026-02-23 - PM Review (Sofia Martinez): Requested explicit UX for 'preview diff' of changes and a clear cancel path. Also asked for telemetry fields for SLO reporting on 'time-to-first-action'.
2026-03-02 - Dev: Added precheck static analysis step to validate templates against schema before assembly. Implemented a fallback guard that marks high-risk steps as 'approval-required'.
2026-03-10 - QA: Began internal e2e tests. Found an edge case where compensation failed when intermediate step mutated a shared resource; added compensation chaining and idempotent marker to schema.
2026-03-10 - Daniel Kim: Security review cleared pending minor KMS integration details. Next: implement execution RBAC hooks and telemetry wiring.
